summary: Lake County, MN: wooden lookout on a hill east of Ely, then an 80-foot steel ladder tower from 1923; survey notes record it removed by 1978; no site description found.

facts.design: 80-foot steel ladder tower; the earlier lookout was wooden
facts.status_note: Survey notes of 1978 say the tower had been removed; the association lists it as gone
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Superior National Forest

events.note: Wooden lookout built by two forest guards, Ole Fernland and John Handberg, and named Fernberg after them. The county table gives 1911; the report's text says late 1910s
80-foot steel ladder tower; steel hauled to the hill in March 1923 under Ranger Frank Carney
County survey notes dated 1978 record the tower as already removed; the removal date itself is not in the sources read

evidence.supports: wooden lookout built by two forest guards in the late 1910s, on a hill several miles east of Ely
evidence.quote: Two forest guards built a wood lookout in the late 1910s or so on a hill several miles east of Ely.
Their names were Ole Fernland and John Handberg.

evidence.supports: the lookout was named Fernberg after the two guards
evidence.quote: lookout was named Fernberg after them.

evidence.supports: the report's table dates the first lookout to 1911
the steel tower was an 80-foot ladder tower, also named after the two guards
evidence.quote: The steel lookout that came to stand on that hill was named after them, an 80 foot ladder tower.

evidence.supports: 1978 survey notes record the tower as removed
evidence.quote: Survey notes - 1978 - Tower has been removed.

evidence.supports: steel for an 80-foot tower hauled to Fernburg hill, 18 miles east of Ely, in March 1923; Ranger Frank Carney, of the Superior National Forest staff, supervising
evidence.quote: Steel for an 80-foot fire lookout tower is this week being hauled to Fernburg hill, a high point 18 miles east of Ely, under the supervision of Ranger Frank Carney, of the Superior National forest staff.

evidence.supports: Minneapolis Star, the next day, said the tower would be erected on Fernburg hill, 18 miles east of Ely
evidence.quote: An 80-foot forest fire lookout tower will be erected on Fernburg hill, 18 miles east of here (Ely).

evidence.supports: the association lists the site as gone, under the name Fernberg Lake

resolved_conflicts.field: events: year of the first (wooden) lookout
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The county table gives 1911; the same report's text says the late 1910s. The story gives both and does not pick one.
The report places the first lookout several miles east of Ely; the 1923 newspapers put the steel tower's hill 18 miles east. The story reports both. They may describe the same hill.
Newspapers of 1923 say Fernburg; the report and the association say Fernberg. The story uses Fernberg, the name in the brief's record.

sources.title: Lake County Minnesota Fire Lookout Towers (report)
sources.publisher: Wikimedia Commons (PDF citing USFS and Minnesota Forest Service records)

sources.title: Fernburg, Forest Lookouts (quoting the Star Tribune and Minneapolis Star, March 1923)

notes_for_editor: Brief record says gone; the association and the county survey notes agree the tower was removed by 1978, but no removal date is given. Two real conflicts, both kept in the story: first lookout year (1911 table vs late 1910s text) and distance from Ely (several miles vs 18 miles). The 80 ft height is converted to 24.4 m from the report's figure. No source read describes the site today, access, staffing, or fires. No photos found. Used one WebSearch and four page reads.
